name: wait
description: Pause for a number of seconds, then continue automatically on the SAME turn. Use this whenever you are waiting on something asynchronous — most importantly an async tool that returned a job_id / a "processing" status (e.g. an MCP image/sound/speech/music generation), a background build, or a server that needs a moment to come up. After the wait returns, immediately take your next action (poll the job, re-check status, read the result). CRITICAL: never just SAY "I'll wait 20s then poll" in prose and stop — writing that text ends your turn and nothing actually waits. To truly wait you MUST call this tool; the loop only resumes after a real tool result. Typical pattern: start job(s) → wait(15) → poll → if still processing, wait(15) → poll again, until done. Max 60 seconds per call; for longer waits, call it repeatedly in a poll loop.

seconds.description: How long to pause, in seconds (1–60). Use ~10–20s between polls of a generation job.

reason.description: Optional short note on what you are waiting for (e.g. "sound effect jobs to finish").
